blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY — The El Niño-induced dry spell has caused an estimated P300 million in agricultural losses in Eastern Visayas, affecting more than 6,400 farmers and nearly 8,000 hectares of farmland, mostly planted with rice, the Department of Agriculture (DA) reported. Rodel Mapacapañas, DA-8 acting regional executive director, said crop yields in affected famrs were reduced. He clarified, however, that farmers in the affected areas were still able to harvest their crops, although production was lower than expected. “Based on our monitoring, most of the nearly 8,000 hectares severely affected by El Niño have still produced harvests, but yields have declined,” […]...
